1  high  A mailbox forwards mail outside your organization (Workspace)
   [workspace.external_forwarding]
   Subject       admin@example.com -> admin.home@gmail.com (mail_forward admin@example.com ->
                 admin.home@gmail.com)
   Observed      g000008 (12:00, as unknown): admin@example.com forwards all incoming mail except
                 spam to admin.home@gmail.com (automatic forwarding is on; after forwarding, Gmail
                 moves the original to Trash, a pattern used to hide forwarded mail from the
                 person). gmail.com is not a domain of this Workspace. scheck read the setting, not
                 whether any message was forwarded.
   Observed      g000020 (12:00, as unknown): admin@example.com forwards all incoming mail except
                 spam to admin.home@gmail.com (automatic forwarding is on; after forwarding, Gmail
                 moves the original to Trash, a pattern used to hide forwarded mail from the
                 person). gmail.com is not a domain of this Workspace. scheck read the setting, not
                 whether any message was forwarded.
   Severity      high: base medium, +1 attribute admin (g000020: admin@example.com is a super
                 administrator: mail sent to administrators, such as security alerts and
                 password-reset links from other services, goes to this mailbox.)
   Why here      admin@example.com is a super administrator: mail sent to administrators, such as
                 security alerts and password-reset links from other services, goes to this mailbox.
   Not checked   Whether any message was forwarded, and what each filter matches, were not checked.
   Fix           Ask the person, in person or by phone rather than by email, whether they set this
                 up and still need it. If they did and still need it, note why and accept it for
                 this address; forwarding to any other address stays open. If not, remove it in the
                 person's Gmail: Settings → See all settings → Forwarding and POP/IMAP (forwarding)
                 and Filters and Blocked Addresses (filters). If nobody set it up, treat the account
                 as possibly taken over and contain it before removing anything, so a live session
                 cannot add it back: sign the account out everywhere, reset its password, revoke its
                 app access and check its 2-step verification; then remove the forwarding, and use
                 Email Log Search in the Admin console to see what was forwarded. To stop forwarding
                 outside the organization for everyone, an administrator can allow automatic
                 forwarding to internal addresses only, or turn it off: Admin console → Apps →
                 Google Workspace → Gmail → End User Access → Automatic forwarding. Afterwards,
                 check that existing forwarding stopped; scheck did not test this.

  saas:google-workspace:example.com: Third-party app access was not checked: the selected Workspace
    profile does not read it. The check lists apps people allowed into their mail, Drive or
    calendar, a common way an attacker keeps access after a phishing email. It needs the Workspace
    permission admin.directory.user.security, which Google offers only together with the ability to
    revoke app access, sign people out and turn off 2-step verification; the checks above do not
    need it. If your organization wants this check, an administrator can approve a dedicated
    credential for it, so the everyday one keeps read-only permissions; then run again with
    SCHECK_WORKSPACE_PROFILE=directory_oauth_mail.

    Security → Access and data control → API controls → Manage Domain Wide Delegation lists
    gmail.readonly.
